verdicts.title: Fully Dynamic Connectivity in $O(\log n(\log\log n)^2)$ Amortized Expected Time
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Dynamic connectivity is one of the most fundamental problems in dynamic graph algorithms. We present a randomized Las Vegas dynamic connectivity data structure with $O(\log n(\log\log n)^2)$ amortized expected update time and $O(\log n/\log\log\log n)$ worst case query time, which comes very close to the cell probe lower bounds of Patrascu and Demaine (2006) and Patrascu and Thorup (2011).
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns a dynamic graph connectivity data structure with $O(\log n(\log\log n)^2)$ update time, sharing only superficial logarithmic asymptotic vocabulary with the conjecture; it makes no claim about geometric Langlands duality or Frege proof complexity.

verdicts.title: An $Ω( (\log n / \log \log n)^2 )$ Cell-Probe Lower Bound for Dynamic Boolean Data Structures
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We resolve the long-standing open problem of Boolean dynamic data structure hardness, proving an unconditional lower bound of $Ω((\log n / \log\log n)^2)$ for the Multiphase Problem of Patrascu [STOC 2010] (instantiated with Inner Product over $\mathbb{F}_2$). This matches the celebrated barrier for weighted problems established by Larsen [STOC 2012] and closes the gap left by the $Ω(\log^{1.5} n)$ Boolean bound of Larsen, Weinstein, and Yu [STOC 2018].

verdicts.title: SceneEval: Evaluating Semantic Coherence in Text-Conditioned 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Despite recent advances in text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation, there remain gaps in the evaluation of these methods. Existing metrics often measure realism by comparing generated scenes to a set of ground-truth scenes, but they overlook how well scenes follow the input text and capture implicit expectations of plausibility.
